subject: Any luck running Sequenza on IonProton data?

messages.author: 484217e7259ff444
messages.subject: Any luck running Sequenza on IonProton data?
parts:
Hi, 

I have a (large) set of plasma DNA-seq data generated on a Life Technologies Ion Proton (targeted seq, relatively low number of genes) and I hope to identify copy number changes and tumour purity from this group. I have germline data for a large number of these.

Does Sequenza work for panel data? Any advice would be greatly appreciated.

Kind regards,
George

messages.author: dad6980b76d10753
messages.subject: Re: Any luck running Sequenza on IonProton data?
parts:
Hi George,

I’m sure it is possible to make it work on some extent, but you need to completely change the running methodology, ie: you will not be able to use the workflow as suggested in the package, or at least you need to heavily tweak the parameters.

First thing: in a panel there are not many heterozygous positions, you should focus on somatic variations; there is a method for that in the sequenza.fit function, It is very slow wot WES or WGS, because of the big number of SNV, but a gene panels would be a perfect use case, I guess. you can try it and see how well it works for you.

I don’t know if the coverage profile of sequencing panels are generally suitable for CNV calls (eg weaving profiles where no copy number change are expected). You should visually inspect the results and evaluate if correspond to a reliable info of not.

the sequenza.results and sequenza.extract are meant for WXS, so you should change almost all the default parameter, in the sequenza.fit, (a part the method argument, as previously suggested) you should surely change the segments filter argument, by default it filters out the segments smaller the 3Mb.

So as you can see there are many unknown, and many things you need to be aware of, but is not impossible, you can quickly work on a test, especially if (by any chance) you have some data with previously known cnv and purity estimates.

Best

Francesco
